# MCP tool catalog

<!-- Generated by bin/surface-catalogs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Generated catalog of MCP tools registered through `McpToolRegistry`.

The Permission column is each tool's consequence classification on that
surface (see [Permission authority](permission_authority.md)):

- **essential** -- consequence-free agent work. Always allowed: it is
  evaluated and audited, but no rule, preset, lease or confirmation request
  can block it. `default: allow` is not essential; internal persistence
  alone is not a consequence barrier.
- **gated** -- crosses a consequence barrier, named by its effects.
- **deniable** -- no barrier effect, but deniable for the named reason.

## Interactive chat tool parity exceptions

Every tool meaningful in an interactive chat is discoverable in planner,
coding, local, and coworker chats unless a reviewed exception below says
the operation is semantically incoherent there. Authorization is never an
exception: risky, admin, destructive, external-write, and credential-using
tools stay shared and rely on canonical permission checks.

| Reason code | Explanation | Owner | Absent from | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workflow_run_bound_verdict` | Verdict/callback tools are bound to one reviewer or workflow run, not an interactive chat. | workflow-engine | `all` | `submit_summary`, `submit_test_plan`, `submit_report`, `patch_workflow`, `submit_adversarial_review`, `submit_security_review`, `submit_visual_review` |
| `workflow_run_bound_verdict` | The coworker review verdict is bound to one reviewer run, not an interactive chat. | coworkers | `all` | `submit_coworker_review` |
| `owner_permission_decision` | A coworker must not grant, deny, lease, or revoke its own permissions; the owner decides. | coworkers | `coworker` | `list_permissions`, `explain_permission`, `grant_permission`, `deny_permission`, `revoke_permission`, `create_permission_lease`, `revoke_permission_lease`, `apply_permission_preset`, `cancel_authorization_request` |
| `coworker_sanitized_surface` | Coworker-scoped repository reads and sanitized diagnostics, authorized by coworker grants. | coworkers | `planner`, `coding`, `local` | `list_repository_files`, `read_repository_file`, `search_repository_code`, `read_backend_exception_events`, `read_browser_error_events`, `read_performance_log_events` |
| `coworker_identity_lifecycle` | Requests addressed to the coworker's owner have no subject outside a coworker chat. | coworkers | `planner`, `coding`, `local` | `discover_coworker_capabilities`, `surrender_permission_lease`, `request_permission_revocation` |
| `requires_coding_checkout` | Needs a Coding Mode checkout or runtime session. | coding-mode | `all` | tools gated to a dedicated chat role |
| `requires_local_checkout` | Needs a Local Mode daemon workspace. | local-mode | `all` | tools gated to a dedicated chat role |
| `evaluator_run_bound` | Bound to the disposable scoped-event evaluator. | chat | `all` | tools gated to a dedicated chat role |
| `syrus_dev_sanitized_diagnostics` | Sanitized Syrus diagnostics are offered through coworker grants; ordinary chats read diagnostics through admin tools. | syrus-dev | `planner`, `coding`, `local` | `read_performance_diagnostics`, `read_syrus_logs` |
| `coworker_identity_lifecycle` | Coworker workspace, reply, schedule and spawn tools operate on a coworker identity that has no non-coworker subject; ordinary chats get only the deferred drafting tools. | coworkers | `planner`, `coding`, `local` | `message_coworker`, `reply_in_chat_thread`, `manage_coworker_schedule`, `spawn_coworker_chat`, `spawn_syrus_chat`, `write_coworker_file`, `edit_coworker_file`, `move_coworker_file`, `delete_coworker_file` |
